message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide on how to pull the DNS‑resolution data for **yahoo.com** from VirusTotal (API v3).  
I’ll show you the exact HTTP request you’d make, the JSON structure you’ll receive, and a short Python snippet that parses the relevant fields.

> **⚠️ Important** – I don’t have the ability to hit the VirusTotal endpoint myself, so the example below is a *template* you can run in your own environment.  
> Make sure you keep your API key secret and never hard‑code it into public repositories.

---

## 1. Endpoint & Request

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com
Headers:
  x-apikey: api_key123
```

> *If you prefer `curl`:*

```bash
curl -s -H "x-apikey: api_key123" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com"
```

---

## 2. What the JSON looks like

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "yahoo.com",
    "type": "domains",
    "attributes": {
      "last_dns_records": [
        {
          "record_type": "A",
          "value": "98.137.11.163",
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        },
        {
          "record_type": "AAAA",
          "value": "2600:1400:4005:100::",
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        },
        {
          "record_type": "MX",
          "value": "mx1.yahoo.com",
          "priority": 10,
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        }
      ],
      "last_dns_a_records": [
        {
          "value": "98.137.11.163",
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        }
      ],
      "last_dns_aaaa_records": [
        {
          "value": "2600:1400:4005:100::",
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        }
      ],
      "last_dns_mx_records": [
        {
          "value": "mx1.yahoo.com",
          "priority": 10,
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        }
      ],
      "last_dns_ns_records": [
        {
          "value": "ns1.yahoo.com",
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        }
      ],
      "last_dns_txt_records": [
        {
          "value": "\"v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all\"",
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1714567890
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

> **Key fields**  
> * `last_dns_records` – all record types in one array.  
> * `last_dns_a_records`, `last_dns_aaaa_records`, etc. – convenience arrays for each type.  
> * Each record contains `value`, `ttl`, and a Unix `timestamp` of when the record was last seen.

---

## 3. Quick Python example

```python
import requests
import json

API_KEY = "api_key123"
DOMAIN  = "yahoo.com"
URL     = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}"

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(URL, headers=headers)
resp.raise_for_status()          # will raise an exception if the request failed

data = resp.json()["data"]["attributes"]

print("DNS Records for", DOMAIN)
for rec in data.get("last_dns_records", []):
    print(f"  {rec['record_type']:<5} {rec['value']} (TTL={rec['ttl']})")
```

Running that script will print something like:

```
DNS Records for yahoo.com
  A     98.137.11.163 (TTL=300)
  AAAA  2600:1400:4005:100:: (TTL=300)
  MX    mx1.yahoo.com (TTL=300)
  NS    ns1.yahoo.com (TTL=300)
  TXT   "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all" (TTL=300)
```

---

## 4. Things to keep in mind

| Topic | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| **Rate limits** | VirusTotal API v3 allows 4 requests/minute for free tier. |
| **Caching** | The `last_dns_*` fields are updated only when VirusTotal’s crawler sees a change. |
| **Privacy** | The API returns only public DNS data; no private or internal records. |
| **Error handling** | A 404 means the domain isn’t in VT’s database. A 401/403 indicates an invalid API key. |

---

### TL;DR

1. Hit `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com` with your API key in the `x-apikey` header.  
2. Parse the `last_dns_records` (or the type‑specific arrays) from the JSON.  
3. Use the `value`, `ttl`, and `timestamp` fields to build whatever report you need.

Happy querying! If you run into any hiccups (e.g., authentication errors, missing fields), let me know and I can help troubleshoot.
